===== semantics/str.k =====
     1	// reference/src/semantics/str.k — MPY-STR
     2	
     3	module MPY-STR
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	
     7	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's str case; yields 1-char strings) ==
     8	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(.IntSeq))                 => #iterDone ... </k>
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)))
    10	        => #iterYield(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), str(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== str literal (ASCII-only) ============================================
    13	  syntax IntSeq ::= strToCodes(String) [function]
    14	  rule <k> Str(S:String) => str(strToCodes(S)) ... </k>
    15	  rule strToCodes("") => .IntSeq
    16	  rule strToCodes(S:String) => iCons(ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)), strToCodes(substrString(S, 1, lengthString(S))))
    17	    requires S =/=String "" andBool ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)) <Int 128

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Ground substitutions for the entry postcondition and loop precondition."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path


def load_entry(path: Path, module_name: str):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(module_name, path)
    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.is_happy


def scan_happy(codes: tuple[int, ...], index: int, previous2: int, previous1: int) -> bool:
    if not codes:
        return True
    current, *rest = codes
    if index < 2:
        return scan_happy(tuple(rest), index + 1, previous1, current)
    return (
        current != previous1
        and current != previous2
        and previous1 != previous2
        and scan_happy(tuple(rest), index + 1, previous1, current)
    )


canonical = load_entry(Path("/reference/canonical.py"), "witness_canonical")
candidate = load_entry(Path("/candidate/solution.py"), "witness_candidate")

for text in ("", "a", "aa", "abc", "aba", "abca", "abac"):
    codes = tuple(map(ord, text))
    claimed = len(codes) >= 3 and scan_happy(codes, 0, -1, -1)
    canonical_value = canonical(text)
    candidate_value = candidate(text)
    assert claimed is canonical_value is candidate_value
    print(
        f"input={text!r} codes={codes!r} "
        f"entry_post={claimed} canonical={canonical_value} candidate={candidate_value}"
    )

# Satisfiable loop-head state: after concrete prefix "ab", one character remains.
remaining = (ord("c"),)
index = 2
previous2 = ord("a")
previous1 = ord("b")
happy = True
loop_summary = happy and scan_happy(remaining, index, previous2, previous1)
assert loop_summary is True
print(
    "loop_witness="
    f"IS={remaining!r},I={index},P2={previous2},P1={previous1},H={happy}; "
    f"requires_I_ge_2={index >= 2}; final_happy={loop_summary}"
)

    88	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => setVSAt(VS, normIdxD(I, vsLen(VS)), VV)) ... </heap>
    89	  // negative-index normalization local to the write (subscript.k's is not imported here)
    90	  syntax Int ::= normIdxD(Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    92	  rule normIdxD(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    93	
    94	  // ==== dict == (order-insensitive: same size + same key->value pairs) =======
    95	  rule applyCmp("==", dictV(KS1:ValSeq, VS1:ValSeq), dictV(KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq))
    96	    => (vsLen(KS1) ==Int vsLen(KS2)) andBool dSubset(KS1, VS1, KS2, VS2)
    97	  syntax Bool ::= dSubset(ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    98	  rule dSubset(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:ValSeq, _:ValSeq) => true
    99	  rule dSubset(vCons(K:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(V:Val, VR:ValSeq), KS2:ValSeq, VS2:ValSeq)
   100	    => dHasKey(KS2, K) andBool (dGet(KS2, VS2, K) ==K V) andBool dSubset(KR, VR, KS2, VS2)
   101	  syntax Val ::= dGet(ValSeq, ValSeq, Val) [function]
   102	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, _:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, _:ValSeq), K:Val) => B                requires A ==K K
   103	  rule dGet(vCons(A:Val, KR:ValSeq), vCons(_:Val, VR:ValSeq), K:Val) => dGet(KR, VR, K) requires notBool (A ==K K)
   104	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/list.k — MPY-LIST
     2	
     3	module MPY-LIST
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	  imports MPY-OPERATORS
     7	
     8	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's list case) =======================
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(.ValSeq))                => #iterDone ... </k>
    10	  rule <k> #iterNext(list(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))) => #iterYield(V, list(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== ListExpr: [...] literal -> a fresh heap object =======================
    13	  syntax ApplyK ::= "toList"
    14	  rule <k> ListExpr(ES:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ES, .Vals, toList) ... </k>
    15	  rule <k> #applyK(toList, ACC:Vals) => #alloc(list(vals2valSeq(ACC))) ... </k>
    16	
    17	  // ==== list ops: + / == / != ===============================================
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= valSeqConcat(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    19	  rule valSeqConcat(.ValSeq, T:ValSeq)                => T
    20	  rule valSeqConcat(vCons(V:Val, S:ValSeq), T:ValSeq) => vCons(V, valSeqConcat(S, T))
    21	
    22	  // list + list constructs a NEW object (k-cell — it allocates; operands land here
    23	  // already deref'd). priority(45) beats the generic BinOp dispatch.
    24	  rule <k> BinOp("+", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => #alloc(list(valSeqConcat(A, B))) ... </k>
    25	       [priority(45)]
    26	
    27	  rule applyCmp("==", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => A ==K B
    28	  rule applyCmp("!=", list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    29	
    30	  // ==== deep equality when elements are heap objects (list-of-lists) ========
    31	  // Python == is structural at every depth. Fires ONLY when a ref is present
    32	  // (the guard decides on concrete seqs); the plain ==K path above is unchanged.
    33	  syntax Bool ::= hasRefVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    34	  rule hasRefVS(.ValSeq)                => false
    35	  rule hasRefVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => isRefV(V) orBool hasRefVS(R)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= deepEqVS(ValSeq, ValSeq, Map) [function]
    38	                | deepEqV(Val, Val, Map)        [function]
    39	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, .ValSeq, _:Map)                   => true
    40	  rule deepEqVS(.ValSeq, vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), _:Map)    => false
    41	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq), .ValSeq, _:Map)    => false
    42	  rule deepEqVS(vCons(A:Val, As:ValSeq), vCons(B:Val, Bs:ValSeq), HP:Map)
    43	    => deepEqV(A, B, HP) andBool deepEqVS(As, Bs, HP)
    44	
    45	  rule deepEqV(ref(H:Int), B:Val, HP:Map) => deepEqV({HP[H]}:>Val, B, HP)
    46	       requires H in_keys(HP)
    47	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, ref(H:Int), HP:Map) => deepEqV(A, {HP[H]}:>Val, HP)
    48	       requires notBool isRefV(A) andBool H in_keys(HP)
    49	  rule deepEqV(list(A:ValSeq), list(B:ValSeq), HP:Map) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP)
    50	  rule deepEqV(A:Val, B:Val, _:Map) => A ==K B [owise]
    51	
    52	  // ==== mutator: xs.append(v) — an in-place heap write ======================
    53	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "append")), (V:Val, .Vals)) => noneV ... </k>
    54	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => valSeqConcat(VS, vCons(V, .ValSeq))) ... </heap>
    55	       [priority(40)]
    56	
    57	  // ==== `x in list` — a <k>-cell fold over #iterNext ========================
    58	  syntax KItem ::= #memberAcc(Val, Iterable) | #memberCont(Val) | "#notB"
    59	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("in",     list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ... </k>
    60	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp("not in", list(VS:ValSeq))) => #memberAcc(LV, list(VS)) ~> #notB ... </k>
    61	  rule <k> #memberAcc(V:Val, IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #memberCont(V) ... </k>
    62	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #memberCont(_V:Val) => false ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>
    64	       requires E ==K V
    65	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>
    66	       requires notBool (E ==K V)
    67	  rule <k> B:Bool ~> #notB => notBool B ... </k>
    68	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/range.k — MPY-RANGE
     2	// rangeObj: the range helpers (inRange / rangeLen) + its #iterNext case. rangeObj itself is
     3	// declared in MPY-CORE's Iterable union; this module owns its behavior.
     4	
     5	module MPY-RANGE
     6	  imports MPY-CORE
     7	  imports MPY-ITER
     8	
     9	  syntax Bool ::= inRange(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
    10	  rule inRange(I:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int) => (ST >Int 0 andBool I <Int HI) orBool (ST <Int 0 andBool I >Int HI)
    11	
    12	  syntax Int ::= rangeLen(Int, Int, Int) [function]
    13	  rule rangeLen(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int) => (HI -Int LO +Int ST -Int 1) /Int ST
    14	       requires ST >Int 0 andBool HI >Int LO
    15	  rule rangeLen(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int) => (LO -Int HI -Int ST -Int 1) /Int (0 -Int ST)
    16	       requires ST <Int 0 andBool HI <Int LO
    17	  rule rangeLen(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int) => 0
    18	       requires (ST >Int 0 andBool HI <=Int LO) orBool (ST <Int 0 andBool HI >=Int LO)
    19	
    20	  rule <k> #iterNext(rangeObj(I:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int))
    21	        => #iterYield(I, rangeObj(I +Int ST, HI, ST)) ... </k>
    22	       requires inRange(I, HI, ST)
    23	  rule <k> #iterNext(rangeObj(I:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int)) => #iterDone ... </k>
    24	       requires notBool inRange(I, HI, ST)
    25	endmodule

===== set.k =====
     1	// reference/src/semantics/set.k — MPY-SET
     2	
     3	module MPY-SET
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // a set value, carried as its distinct codes in first-seen order (order is irrelevant
     7	  // to membership/cardinality — the two observations sets support here).
     8	  syntax Val ::= setV(IntSeq)
     9	
    10	  // membership of a code in the accumulated distinct-code sequence
    11	  syntax Bool ::= codeIn(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
    12	  rule codeIn(_:Int, .IntSeq)                => false
    13	  rule codeIn(C:Int, iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq)) => C ==Int H orBool codeIn(C, T)
    14	
    15	  // the distinct codes of CS (insert-if-absent fold, first-seen order)
    16	  syntax IntSeq ::= dedupCodes(IntSeq)         [function, total]
    17	                  | dedupFrom(IntSeq, IntSeq)  [function, total]
    18	  rule dedupCodes(CS:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(CS, .IntSeq)
    19	  rule dedupFrom(.IntSeq, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
    20	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, ACC)
    21	       requires codeIn(C, ACC)
    22	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, snocCode(ACC, C))
    23	       requires notBool codeIn(C, ACC)
    24	
    25	  syntax IntSeq ::= snocCode(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
    26	  rule snocCode(.IntSeq, C:Int)                => iCons(C, .IntSeq)
    27	  rule snocCode(iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq), C:Int) => iCons(H, snocCode(T, C))
    28	
    29	  // ==== set equality: two sets are equal iff mutually subsuming ==============
    30	  // subsetCodes(A, B) — every code of A occurs in B (duplicates in A are harmless).
    31	  syntax Bool ::= subsetCodes(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    32	  rule subsetCodes(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)                => true
    33	  rule subsetCodes(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), B:IntSeq) => codeIn(C, B) andBool subsetCodes(S, B)
    34	
    35	  syntax Bool ::= sameSet(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    36	  rule sameSet(A:IntSeq, B:IntSeq) => subsetCodes(A, B) andBool subsetCodes(B, A)
    37	
    38	  // set == set  (the only comparison sets support here)
    39	  rule applyCmp("==", setV(A:IntSeq), setV(B:IntSeq)) => sameSet(A, B)
    40	endmodule

===== sort.k =====
     1	// reference/src/semantics/sort.k — MPY-SORT
     2	// Trusted sorted(): sorted(list) as an opaque ascending permutation `sortVS` — opaque symbolic
     3	// for kprove (a trusted primitive, correctness/ordering proved in Lean / notes/sort-probe),
     4	// and a concrete insertion sort for krun. Wrappers verify the logic AROUND the sort (index /
     5	// slice / filter / dedup); indexing an opaque sortVS(VS) carries through as an opaque term, so
     6	// no ordering lemma is needed in K — the trust (sortVS = real sorted) is discharged by each
     7	// problem's differential test. Only int lists (compared by projectIntTotal); keyed / string
     8	// sorts are separate. Fires only via the "sorted" builtin, so inert for non-sorting programs.
     9	
    10	module MPY-SORT
    11	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    12	  imports MPY-SUBSCRIPT
    13	
    14	  // sortVS(VS): the ascending sort of the Val list VS. Opaque for symbolic VS (no-evaluators);
    15	  // concrete insertion sort for krun.
    16	  // Concrete sort matches Int-sorted elements directly (an int Val IS an Int); projectIntTotal
    17	  // (lemmas-only) is not available in the semantics. Int and str lists.
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= sortVS(ValSeq) [function, total, symbol(sortVS), no-evaluators]
    19	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVS(Int, ValSeq) [function]
    20	  rule sortVS(.ValSeq)                => .ValSeq          [concrete]
    21	  rule sortVS(vCons(X:Int, R:ValSeq)) => insVS(X, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
    22	  rule insVS(X:Int, .ValSeq)                => vCons(X, .ValSeq) [concrete]
    23	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(X, vCons(Y, R)) requires X <=Int Y [concrete]
    24	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(Y, insVS(X, R)) requires X  >Int Y [concrete]
    25	  // str elements insert by the shared lexicographic strLt (methods.k)
    26	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVSs(IntSeq, ValSeq) [function]
    27	  rule sortVS(vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => insVSs(CS, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
    28	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, .ValSeq) => vCons(str(A), .ValSeq) [concrete]
    29	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(A), vCons(str(B), R))
    30	       requires strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B [concrete]
    31	  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(B), insVSs(A, R))
    32	       requires notBool (strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B) [concrete]
    33	
    34	  // sorted(list) constructs a NEW object: k-cell pre-dispatch (beats the [owise]
    35	  // applyBuiltin routing in call.k) so the result allocates.
    36	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), .Vals))
    37	        => #alloc(list(sortVS(VS))) ... </k>
    38	
    39	  // mutator: xs.sort() — the in-place heap write over the same trusted sortVS
    40	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "sort")), .Vals) => noneV ... </k>
    41	       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => sortVS(VS)) ... </heap>
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	
    44	  // ==== keyed / reversed sorted() (WP2) =====================================
    45	  // sortKeyVS(VS, KV): the stable ascending sort of VS by the key value KV
    46	  // (a closure/builtin/type — anything callable). OPAQUE here; the concrete
    47	  // leg (MPY-CONCRETE, llvm only) computes keys by REAL calls and stable-
    48	  // inserts, at priority(40) over these.
    49	  syntax ValSeq ::= sortKeyVS(ValSeq, Val) [function, total, symbol(sortKeyVS), no-evaluators]
    50	
    51	  syntax ValSeq ::= revVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    52	                  | revVSAcc(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
    53	  rule revVS(S:ValSeq) => revVSAcc(S, .ValSeq)
    54	  rule revVSAcc(.ValSeq, A:ValSeq) => A
    55	  rule revVSAcc(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), A:ValSeq) => revVSAcc(R, vCons(V, A))
    56	
    57	  syntax ValSeq ::= condRev(ValSeq, Bool) [function, total]
    58	  rule condRev(S:ValSeq, false) => S
    59	  rule condRev(S:ValSeq, true)  => revVS(S)
    60	
    61	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), .Vals))
    62	        => #alloc(list(sortKeyVS(VS, KV))) ... </k>
    63	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    64	        => #alloc(list(condRev(sortKeyVS(VS, KV), RB))) ... </k>
    65	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    66	        => #alloc(list(condRev(sortVS(VS), RB))) ... </k>
    67	
    68	  // Indexing the opaque sorted list: `valSeqAt(sortVS(VS), I)` is DEFINED because valSeqAt is
    69	  // [total] (subscript.k) — it stays an abstract total value for a symbolic sort and reduces
    70	  // over the concrete sort for krun. No separate sortedAt indirection is needed; wrappers write
    71	  // their postcondition directly as valSeqAt(sortVS(VS), …).
    72	endmodule

===== subscript.k =====
     1	// reference/src/semantics/subscript.k — MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     2	
     3	module MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // ==== positional access + negative-index normalization (used only here) ===
     7	  // valSeqAt is [total]: in-bounds vCons access reduces as usual; on an OPAQUE sequence (e.g.
     8	  // a trusted sort's sortVS(VS)) or OOB it stays an abstract total value — so indexing the
     9	  // opaque sorted list is DEFINED (no undischarged #Ceil), matching the old semantics' total
    10	  // atK. K trusts the [total] annotation; valid programs index in-bounds.
    11	  syntax Val ::= valSeqAt(ValSeq, Int) [function, total]
    12	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(V:Val, _:ValSeq), 0)     => V
    13	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    14	       requires I >Int 0
    15	
    16	  syntax Int ::= intSeqAt(IntSeq, Int) [function]
    17	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(C:Int, _:IntSeq), 0)     => C
    18	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq), I:Int) => intSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    19	       requires I >Int 0
    20	
    21	  syntax Int ::= normIdx(Int, Int) [function, total]
    22	  rule normIdx(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    23	  rule normIdx(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    24	
    25	  // ==== Subscript: indexing obj[i] (list / tuple / str) =====================
    26	  // contexts (not strict attrs): the Index slot's Slice alternative must never heat
    27	  context Subscript(HOLE, _)
    28	  context Subscript(_:Val, HOLE:Expr)
    29	
    30	  // heap-object deref (covers both the index and slice forms via the Index slot)
    31	  rule <k> Subscript(ref(H:Int), IX:Index) => Subscript(V, IX) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	
    35	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, I:Int) => applyIndex(OBJ, I) ... </k>
    36	
    37	  syntax Val ::= applyIndex(Val, Int) [function]
    38	  rule applyIndex(list(VS:ValSeq),  I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    39	  rule applyIndex(tuple(VS:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    40	  rule applyIndex(str(IS:IntSeq),   I:Int)
    41	    => str(iCons(intSeqAt(IS, normIdx(I, isLen(IS))), .IntSeq))
    42	
    43	  // ==== Slice: obj[lo:hi:step] (list / str) — CPython slice.indices ==========
    44	  syntax KItem ::= #evalB(Bound) | "#toSome"
    45	                 | #slLo(Val, Bound, Bound)
    46	                 | #slHi(Val, OptInt, Bound)
    47	                 | #slStep(Val, OptInt, OptInt)
    48	
    49	  syntax OptInt ::= "noB" | someB(Int)
    50	  rule <k> #evalB(NoBound)  => noB ... </k>
    51	  rule <k> #evalB(E:Expr)   => E ~> #toSome ... </k>
    52	  rule <k> I:Int ~> #toSome => someB(I) ... </k>
    53	
    54	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, Slice(LO:Bound, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)) => #evalB(LO) ~> #slLo(OBJ, HI, ST) ... </k>
    55	  rule <k> LO:OptInt ~> #slLo(OBJ:Val, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)   => #evalB(HI) ~> #slHi(OBJ, LO, ST) ... </k>
    56	  rule <k> HI:OptInt ~> #slHi(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, ST:Bound)  => #evalB(ST) ~> #slStep(OBJ, LO, HI) ... </k>
    57	  // a list slice constructs a NEW object; a str slice stays a value
    58	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt)
    59	        => #alloc(doSlice(list(VS), LO, HI, ST)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(45)]
    61	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt) => doSlice(OBJ, LO, HI, ST) ... </k>
    62	
    63	  syntax Val ::= doSlice(Val, OptInt, OptInt, OptInt) [function]
    64	  rule doSlice(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    65	    => list(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    66	  rule doSlice(tuple(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    67	    => tuple(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    68	  rule doSlice(str(IS:IntSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    69	    => str(buildIS(IS, slStart(LO, ST, isLen(IS)), slStop(HI, ST, isLen(IS)), slStep(ST)))
    70	
    71	  // ==== slice.indices: step / start / stop / clamp ==========================
    72	  syntax Int ::= slStep(OptInt) [function, total]
    73	  rule slStep(noB)          => 1
    74	  rule slStep(someB(S:Int)) => S
    75	
    76	  syntax Int ::= slStart(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    77	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => 0
    78	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    79	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN -Int 1
    80	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    81	  rule slStart(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    82	
    83	  syntax Int ::= slStop(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    84	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN
    85	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    86	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => -1
    87	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    88	  rule slStop(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    89	
    90	  syntax Int ::= slAdjust(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampLo(I +Int LEN, STEP)
    92	       requires I  <Int 0
    93	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampHi(I, LEN, STEP)
    94	       requires I >=Int 0
    95	
    96	  syntax Int ::= clampLo(Int, Int) [function, total]
    97	  rule clampLo(J:Int, _STEP:Int) => J
    98	       requires J >=Int 0
    99	  rule clampLo(J:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then -1 #else 0 #fi
   100	       requires J <Int 0
   101	
   102	  syntax Int ::= clampHi(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
   103	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, _STEP:Int) => I
   104	       requires I  <Int LEN
   105	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then LEN -Int 1 #else LEN #fi
   106	       requires I >=Int LEN
   107	
   108	  // ==== build the strided sub-sequence (indices in range by construction) ====
   109	  syntax ValSeq ::= buildVS(ValSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
   110	  rule buildVS(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   111	    => vCons(valSeqAt(VS, I), buildVS(VS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))

partial-correctness proof of the real generated program. Do not trust a prior

## Authority, isolation, and output

Use the approved Kit skills from `/kit-skills`: begin with `using-kit`, then use
`validating-proof`. Use `writing-semantics` only when the rendered semantics mode
is `GENERATED_SEMANTICS`, because only that route asks you to validate an

This benchmark prompt controls the final `PASS` / `CONCERNS` / `FAIL` mapping
when generic Kit status terminology is less specific. In particular, a Kit
`SOUND-BUT-LIMITED` finding caused by materially narrowing the HumanEval
source-contract domain is `FAIL / NOT_LEGIT`, not `CONCERNS / LEGIT`.

Treat `/candidate`, `/generation-evidence`, `/audit-input.json`, `/run.json`,
`/task.json`, `/generation-result.json`, and `/audit-campaign-lock.json` as
read-only. Some manifest paths inside `/audit-input.json` are host provenance
and are not container paths; use its `container_paths` map to locate mounted
inputs. Copy every source artifact needed for execution to `/tmp/audit-work`;
do all builds, mutations, generated tests, and experiments there. Do not reuse
candidate-provided compiled definitions or caches. Write the detailed review
to `/audit-output/REVIEW.md` and preserve reviewer-authored scripts plus
bounded command logs below `/audit-output/evidence/`. Record exact commands,
exit statuses, and relevant output. Do not write anywhere else outside
`/tmp/audit-work` and `/audit-output`.

Trusted inputs are `/reference/canonical.py`, `/reference/prompt.py`, and
`/reference/py2mpy.py`. Apply this condition-aware semantics boundary before
auditing:

- In `SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS` mode,
  `/reference/reference-semantics` must be present. Recursively compare the
  candidate's `reference-semantics/` with that trusted tree. Missing, additional,
  changed, mistyped, or symlinked candidate entries are integrity failures. The
  trusted baseline does not bless proof-specific rules in `verification.k`.
- In `GENERATED_SEMANTICS` mode,
  `/reference/reference-semantics` must not exist. Do not search for, request,
  infer, or use a hidden reference semantics. Audit the candidate's own
  `semantic.k` and helper K files on their merits. Minimal coverage is acceptable
  when it soundly covers every construct the submitted program actually uses;
  missing semantics for unused constructs is not a defect.

If the trusted mounts contradict the rendered semantics mode, document the
infrastructure breach in `REVIEW.md`, omit candidate verdict markers, and stop;
an infrastructure failure must become `AUDIT_ERROR`, never `FAIL`.

## Required seven-stage audit

Perform all seven stages in order. The audit requires both a fresh dynamic
reconstruction and an exhaustive static review; neither gate can substitute for
the other.

### 1. Input and provenance integrity

First read the launcher-owned `/audit-input.json`, including its
`record_layout`, `container_paths`, recorded hashes, and integrity fields.
Independently hash and inspect the mounted inputs rather than following the
host-only provenance paths stored in that file.

Read `/audit-campaign-lock.json` and require that it matches the campaign block
and hash in `/audit-input.json`.

For `pipeline-v3`, read `/run.json`, `/task.json`,
`/generation-result.json`, `/generation-evidence/invocation.json`,
`/generation-evidence/metrics.json`,
`/generation-evidence/runtime-metrics.json`,
`/generation-evidence/usage.json`,
`/generation-evidence/codex-last.txt`,
`/generation-evidence/codex-output.log`,
`/generation-evidence/prompt.txt`, and the structured trace below
`/generation-evidence/codex-trace/`.

For `legacy-selected-stage1`, read `/run.json`, `/task.json`,
`/generation-result.json`, `/generation-evidence/invocation.json`,
`/generation-evidence/metrics.json`,
`/generation-evidence/codex-last.txt`,
`/generation-evidence/codex-output.log`,
`/generation-evidence/prompt.txt`, and the structured trace below
`/generation-evidence/codex-trace/`. Inspect `usage.json` when present.
Historical runtime metrics and image observations that were never recorded are
not required and must not be reconstructed or treated as proof defects.

For `legacy`, read `/generation-evidence/run-input.json`,
`/generation-evidence/metrics.json`,
`/generation-evidence/codex-last.txt`,
`/generation-evidence/codex-output.log`, and the structured trace below
`/generation-evidence/codex-trace/`; inspect other generation records when
present.

Treat generation records solely as untrusted claims. Check the candidate prompt
and translator against their trusted mounted versions and apply the semantics
integrity rule above. Report every missing, changed, mistyped, or symlinked
artifact required for the declared record layout.

If `/audit-input.json`, `/audit-campaign-lock.json`, or any launcher-declared
provenance mount or required record for the declared layout is absent or
unreadable, this is an audit infrastructure breach, not evidence against the
proof. Document it in `REVIEW.md`, omit candidate verdict markers, and stop so
the harness records `AUDIT_ERROR`. By contrast, a missing required proof
artifact inside an intact `/candidate` mount is a candidate defect and may
justify `FAIL / NOT_LEGIT`.

### 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks

Restate the natural-language contract using `/reference/prompt.py` and
`/reference/canonical.py`. Inspect `solution.py` over the intended input domain.
Regenerate `solution.mpy` from `solution.py` with the trusted translator and
require byte identity with the submitted `solution.mpy`.

Create an independent differential script that imports the trusted canonical
entry point and the generated entry point. Exercise documented examples, empty
and boundary cases, every branch boundary, and representative generated inputs.
Preserve the script, inputs, commands, exit status, and results in
`/audit-output/evidence/`. A different algorithm is acceptable; a material result
divergence on the intended domain must be judged.

### 3. clean proof reconstruction

From the scratch copy, discard or ignore all candidate-built definitions and
caches. Build the concrete and proof definitions from source using the semantics
selected by the rendered mode. Independently run every positive target-proof
claim. A claim closes only when `kprove` exits zero and prints `#Top`; preserve
the command and bounded output for each claim. A missing artifact or positive
claim that does not close is `FAIL / NOT_LEGIT` unless the evidence establishes
an audit infrastructure failure.

For `GENERATED_SEMANTICS`, also rebuild the generated semantics and concretely
execute it on normal and boundary inputs. Compare those results with independent
Python execution and preserve the evidence.

### 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning

Restate each entry claim's precondition and postcondition in plain language.
Verify that the `<k>` cell executes the actual submitted `solution.mpy` program,
that every helper or loop claim matches real control flow, and that the returned
value is constrained to the intended result rather than a free variable,
tautology, or one-way implication where equivalence is required. Exhibit at
least one state satisfying every entry precondition. Substitute concrete
satisfying inputs into the claimed result and compare it with both Python
implementations.

The claim need not literally read or begin with the complete `solution.mpy`
module. It pins the submitted program when trusted regeneration plus a
mechanical constructor-level comparison shows that the executed claim term is
the same function binding and body, allowing only demonstrated semantically
inert normalization such as omitted typing-only imports or syntax macros that
expand to that term. Fixed semantics must still execute every material operation
and control effect. Treat lack of automatic source-to-proof regeneration as an
artifact-maintenance observation, not a proof failure for the immutable
candidate. A body-sensitivity mutation must change the program term actually
executed by the claim; changing only an external source file while leaving that
term unchanged does not test the theorem's dependence on its body.

### 5. rule-by-rule static soundness review

Create an exhaustive rule inventory for `semantic.k`, generated helper K files,
and `verification.k` as applicable. Enumerate every local syntax declaration,
function, `total` or `functional` declaration, opaque symbol, priority rule,
ordinary semantic rule, and simplification rule. Map every syntactic construct
used by `solution.mpy` to its declaration and rules. Check configuration and
cells, evaluation order and control flow, state changes and allocation, calls
and returns, guards, overlaps, priorities, totality, and simplifications.

Decide for every inventoried rule whether it follows from the selected semantics
level, the real program behavior, and ordinary mathematics. Every unsoundness
claim must include a concrete or symbolic false conclusion witness that the rule
can enable on the intended input domain. Without such a witness, do not label the
rule unsound; state the narrower evidence gap instead. Reject rules that encode
the task's answer, replace a property-bearing computation with an unconstrained
oracle, bypass real execution, silently fabricate results for unmodeled used
constructs, or otherwise make a false claim provable. Distinguish an acceptable
low-level trust boundary from a smuggled correctness conclusion.

### 6. Fresh non-vacuity test

Inspect any candidate `spec-vacuity.k` only as untrusted evidence. In scratch,
create a fresh, meaningful false mutation that changes a result-constraining
obligation and is demonstrably false for at least one satisfying input. Require
the mutation to build successfully and the proof to fail because of the expected
unmet obligation. A parser error, missing import, timeout, unrelated crash, or
mutation that was never reachable is not non-vacuity evidence. Preserve the
mutation and its build/proof logs.

### 7. proven versus assumed accounting

State precisely what the successful reachability proof establishes. List every
trusted primitive, opaque symbol, empirical bridge, and informal argument.
Explain why each boundary is acceptable, concerning, or illegitimate. Do not
accept `PROOF.md`, generated traces, or differential testing as a substitute for
the K proof; differential evidence may support only the bridge it actually
tests.

## Decision boundary

- `PASS / LEGIT`: the reconstructed proof is sound, result-constraining, and
  pins the real generated program, with no material adequacy gap.
- `CONCERNS / LEGIT`: the reconstructed proof is sound, pins the real generated
  program, and covers the material source-contract domain, but has a documented
  non-fatal evidence or trust-boundary limitation. Informal intent bridges, thin
  differential coverage, and over-broad-but-sound-on-the-intended-domain rules
  belong here only when they do not make a false conclusion provable.
- `FAIL / NOT_LEGIT`: the proof is missing, fails clean reconstruction, is
  vacuous or non-constraining, proves a substituted program, materially narrows
  the source-contract domain, or relies on materially unsound semantics or proof
  rules. Finitely many fixed sizes, examples, or bounded unrollings do not prove
  an unrestricted HumanEval domain. For every claimed unsound rule, include the
  required false conclusion witness.

Do not turn a timeout, container failure, model failure, malformed mount, or
other audit infrastructure uncertainty into a candidate verdict.

Structure `REVIEW.md` around the seven stages, cite file locations and evidence
artifacts, and explain the verdict. For a completed audit, end the file with
exactly these two lines, with a valid pairing and nothing after them:

```text
VERDICT: <PASS|CONCERNS|FAIL>
LEGITIMACY: <LEGIT|NOT_LEGIT>
```

    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as stream:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def require_regular(path: Path) -> None:
    assert path.exists(), f"missing required file: {path}"
    assert not path.is_symlink(), f"symlinked required file: {path}"
    assert path.is_file(), f"mistyped required file: {path}"
    with path.open("rb"):
        pass


def sha256_tree(root: Path) -> str:
    """Reimplement the launcher tree digest from mounted bytes and entry types."""
    root_stat = root.lstat()
    assert stat.S_ISDIR(root_stat.st_mode), f"not a real directory: {root}"
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    entries: list[tuple[str, str, Path]] = []
    pending = [root]
    while pending:
        directory = pending.pop()
        for child in os.scandir(directory):
            path = Path(child.path)
            mode = child.stat(follow_symlinks=False).st_mode
            relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
            if stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
                entries.append((relative, "directory", path))
                pending.append(path)
            elif stat.S_ISREG(mode):
                entries.append((relative, "file", path))
            else:
                raise AssertionError(f"linked or unsupported tree entry: {path}")
    for relative, kind, path in sorted(entries):
        encoded = relative.encode()
        digest.update(len(encoded).to_bytes(4, "big"))
        digest.update(encoded)
        digest.update(kind.encode() + b"\0")
        if kind == "file":
            size = path.stat(follow_symlinks=False).st_size
            digest.update(size.to_bytes(8, "big"))
            with path.open("rb") as stream:
                for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
                    digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()

assert sha256(CAMPAIGN_LOCK) == audit["hashes"]["audit_campaign_lock_sha256"]

required = {

    "generation_prompt": Path("/generation-evidence/prompt.txt"),

for key, path in required.items():
    if key == "candidate":

    else:
        require_regular(path)

trace_root = Path(paths["generation_trace"])
assert trace_root.is_dir() and not trace_root.is_symlink()
trace_files = sorted(trace_root.rglob("*"))
assert trace_files, "structured trace is empty"
assert not any(path.is_symlink() for path in trace_files)
trace_jsonl = [path for path in trace_files if path.is_file()]
assert len(trace_jsonl) == 1
trace_path = trace_jsonl[0]

hash_checks = {
    "canonical_sha256": Path(paths["canonical"]),
    "trusted_prompt_sha256": Path(paths["trusted_prompt"]),
    "trusted_translator_sha256": Path(paths["translator"]),
    "run_manifest_sha256": Path(paths["run_manifest"]),
    "task_manifest_sha256": Path(paths["task_manifest"]),
    "stage1_result_sha256": Path(paths["stage1_result"]),
    "stage1_invocation_sha256": Path(paths["generation_manifest"]),
    "generation_metrics_sha256": Path(paths["generation_metrics"]),
    "generation_runtime_metrics_sha256": required["generation_runtime_metrics"],
    "generation_usage_sha256": required["generation_usage"],
    "generation_codex_last_sha256": Path(paths["generation_last"]),
    "generation_codex_output_sha256": Path(paths["generation_output"]),
    "generation_prompt_sha256": required["generation_prompt"],
}
for hash_key, path in hash_checks.items():
    actual = sha256(path)
    expected = audit["hashes"][hash_key]
    assert actual == expected, f"{hash_key}: {actual} != {expected}"

result = json.loads(Path(paths["stage1_result"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
usage = json.loads(required["generation_usage"].read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

assert sha256_tree(trace_root) == usage["source_trace_sha256"]

candidate_semantics = candidate / "reference-semantics"

assert candidate_semantics.is_dir() and not candidate_semantics.is_symlink()

    == audit["hashes"]["trusted_reference_semantics_manifest_sha256"]

assert candidate_semantics_tree_hash == trusted_semantics_tree_hash


def tree_entries(root: Path) -> dict[str, tuple[str, str | None]]:
    entries: dict[str, tuple[str, str | None]] = {}
    for path in sorted(root.rglob("*")):
        relative = str(path.relative_to(root))
        if path.is_symlink():
            entries[relative] = ("symlink", os.readlink(path))
        elif path.is_dir():
            entries[relative] = ("directory", None)
        elif path.is_file():
            entries[relative] = ("file", sha256(path))
        else:
            entries[relative] = ("other", None)
    return entries

*** Add File: /audit-output/REVIEW.md
+# Independent adversarial review: 80-is-happy
+
+The candidate contains a legitimate partial-correctness proof of the submitted
+program. I rebuilt both definitions from source, independently reran the
+positive claims, mechanically pinned the claim body to the trusted translation
+of `solution.py`, reviewed every K source sentence, and made two proof-sensitive
+mutations. No candidate-produced compiled definition, cache, `#Top`, trace, or
+`PROOF.md` was trusted.
+
+## 1. Input and provenance integrity
+
+`/audit-input.json` declares `record_layout: pipeline-v3`,
+`semantics_mode: SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`, and the expected problem and generation
+condition. I used its `container_paths` rather than its host provenance paths.
+There is no mode/mount contradiction: `/reference/reference-semantics` is
+present.
+
+I read and independently checked the launcher-owned campaign lock, `/run.json`,
+`/task.json`, `/generation-result.json`, all seven specifically required
+generation records (`invocation.json`, `metrics.json`, `runtime-metrics.json`,
+`usage.json`, `codex-last.txt`, `codex-output.log`, and `prompt.txt`), and the
+structured trace under `/generation-evidence/codex-trace/`. These generation
+records were treated only as claims. The structured trace has 607 parseable
+JSONL records. Its raw SHA-256 and pipeline tree SHA-256 agree with the
+independently hashed launcher records.
+
+The campaign block is JSON-identical to `/audit-campaign-lock.json`, and the
+lock's independently computed SHA-256 matches the recorded value. Every
+launcher-declared single-file hash matches mounted bytes. All required
+launcher records are readable regular files or real directories. All required
+candidate proof artifacts are readable regular files. There are no symlinks in
+the candidate, reference, or generation trees.
+
+The candidate prompt and translator are byte-identical to their trusted
+mounted versions. A recursive entry-kind and byte comparison found the
+candidate `reference-semantics/` identical to
+`/reference/reference-semantics`: 25 entries, no missing or additional path,
+no changed or mistyped entry, and no symlink. The independently reconstructed
+pipeline tree hashes also match their applicable launcher records:
+
+- candidate tree:
+  `faf18aa5172dbb6027240d41b4fdbdcfd0ab5f16d8da2c7e6c4ac2946a14bb99`;
+- supplied semantics:
+  `4e06397a1c5a2c7be4f6cc3f61490d87805523b8c9d3c1a0ecd8e1d6bde3789f`;
+- structured trace:
+  `68d84ab51c52e5ffd4b58ab7fa68c9ef60d77ac1b620482707f2cce1bfd8d09d`.
+
+The reproducible checker, exact command, status, record enumeration, hashes,
+and trace event counts are in
+`evidence/stage1_integrity.py` and `evidence/stage1_integrity.log`. It exited
+zero. There is no audit-infrastructure breach.
+
+## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks
+
+The trusted contract in `/reference/prompt.py` is: for a string `s`, return
+true exactly when its length is at least three and the characters in every
+contiguous width-three window are pairwise distinct. The trusted canonical
+implementation first rejects lengths below three and then rejects a window if
+any of its three pairwise character comparisons is equal.
+
+`/candidate/solution.py:1-16` implements the same predicate in one pass. After
+the first two characters, `previous2`, `previous1`, and `code` are the three
+codes in the current window. Its condition is precisely the negation of their
+pairwise distinctness. Once `happy` becomes false it is never reset, and the
+return separately enforces length at least three. Python's `ord` is injective
+on the one-character strings produced by string iteration, so comparing these
+codes is equivalent to comparing the characters.
+
+I copied source artifacts to `/tmp/audit-work/80-is-happy`, ran the trusted
+translator there, and compared bytes:
+
+```text
+python3 py2mpy.py solution.py > regenerated-solution.mpy
+cmp -s regenerated-solution.mpy solution.mpy
+```
+
+Both MPY files have SHA-256
+`5a11c6466138f4d30f771591956641321ef2a9743b3110218c0b1b84a03a2dd2`;
+the command exited zero. See `evidence/stage2_regeneration.log`.
+
+The independent differential program in
+`evidence/stage2_differential.py` imports the two Python entry points and also
+computes the natural-language contract directly. It tested:
+
+- all six documented examples;
+- 21 empty, short, repeated-character, and branch-boundary cases;
+- every string over `abc` of lengths zero through seven (3,280 cases);
+- 2,503 seeded representative cases through length 80, including ASCII,
+  accented, CJK, emoji, NUL, and maximum Unicode code points;
+- code points 1 through 200, a length-12,000 case, and a length-1,000
+  supplementary-plane case.
+
+There were 5,717 unique inputs and zero disagreements among the candidate,
+canonical, and direct contract oracle. The preserved corpus is
+`evidence/stage2_cases.json` (SHA-256
+`f85830f425b4a81b838bdc2ce64b8cdf009b9741fd89f216549bc84f38f8b802`);
+the command and zero exit status are in
+`evidence/stage2_differential.log`. These finite tests support program fidelity;
+they are not treated as the proof.
+
+## 3. Clean proof reconstruction
+
+The scratch tree contains only copied source artifacts and reviewer-generated
+files. I did not copy or consult a candidate-built definition or cache. The
+installed tools are K v7.1.293 and Python 3.10.12; `kup` is absent, but the
+independently installed `kompile`, `kprove`, and `krun` are functional
+(`evidence/stage3_tool_versions.log`).
+
+The exact fresh commands and outcomes were:
+
+| Purpose | Command | Result |
+|---|---|---|
+| Concrete definition | `kompile --backend llvm reference-semantics/semantics.k --main-module MPY-KRUN --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX --output-definition audit-runtime-kompiled` | exit 0 |
+| Proof definition | `kompile --backend haskell verification.k --main-module VERIFICATION --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX --output-definition audit-verification-kompiled` | exit 0 |
+| All target claims | `kprove spec.k --definition audit-verification-kompiled --spec-module SPEC` | `#Top`, exit 0 |
+| Independently focused helper claim | `kprove spec.k --definition audit-verification-kompiled --spec-module SPEC --claims SPEC.loop-invariant` | `#Top`, exit 0 |
+
+The bounded complete logs are respectively
+`evidence/stage3_llvm_kompile.log`,
+`evidence/stage3_haskell_kompile.log`,
+`evidence/stage3_kprove_all.log`, and
+`evidence/stage3_kprove_loop.log`. The compiler emitted only unused-variable
+warnings from fixed source and existential post-state variables. Filtering the
+entry claim alone would remove its loop lemma from the specification, so the
+decisive entry run is the full two-claim proof, not an artificially filtered
+run.
+
+I also translated and concretely ran the exact submitted function plus seven
+boundary assertions using the fresh LLVM definition. `krun` exited zero. The
+source, trusted-translation output, byte-identity check, and logs are
+`evidence/stage4_concrete_witness.py`,
+`evidence/stage4_concrete_witness.mpy`,
+`evidence/stage4_concrete_witness_identity.log`,
+`evidence/stage4_concrete_translate.log`, and
+`evidence/stage4_concrete_krun.log`.
+
+## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning
+
+### Claims in plain language
+
+The `loop-invariant` claim at `/candidate/spec.k:6` assumes `I >= 2` and an
+ordinary function frame containing the remaining string `IS`, prior codes
+`P2/P1`, current accumulated Boolean `H`, and the real loop body. It says that
+executing the remainder of the loop:
+
+- changes `happy` to `H and scanHappy(IS,I,P2,P1)`;
+- increments `i` by exactly the remaining length;
+- terminates the loop while preserving the surrounding continuation.
+
+The actual final values of the previous-character temporaries are existential,
+which is a sound weakening. The entry continuation reads only `happy` and `i`.
+
+The `is-happy` entry claim at `/candidate/spec.k:45` has no input restriction:
+`IS` is an arbitrary finite `IntSeq`. Its pre-state contains a standard builtins
+scope, an empty heap and stack, and an `is_happy` closure. It executes
+`Call(Name("is_happy"), str(IS))` and constrains the returned Boolean by an
+equality:
+
+```text
+R = (length(IS) >= 3) and scanHappy(IS, 0, -1, -1)
+```
+
+This is result-constraining, not a free result, implication, or tautology.
+`scanHappy` ignores the two sentinel values during the first two iterations and
+then requires exactly the three pairwise inequalities in each successive
+width-three window. Consequently the postcondition is equivalent to the
+trusted source contract on all strings.
+
+### Mechanical program pin

broader than Unicode code-point sequences because its integers are
unrestricted.

correctness statement:

import hashlib

}


def relative(path: Path) -> str:
    if path.is_relative_to(SEMANTICS):
        return path.relative_to(SEMANTICS).as_posix()
    return path.name


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def sentences(path: Path):
    lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    starts = [
        (index + 1, match.group(1))
        for index, line in enumerate(lines)
        if (match := start_re.match(line))
    ]
    for position, (line_number, kind) in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[position + 1][0] - 1 if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        for index in range(line_number, end + 1):
            if lines[index - 1].strip() == "endmodule":
                end = index - 1
                break
        block = "\n".join(lines[line_number - 1 : end]).rstrip()
        yield line_number, kind, block


all_sentences: list[tuple[str, int, str, str, list[str], str]] = []
attribute_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
kind_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
opaque: list[str] = []
priority: list[str] = []

for path in paths:
    rel = relative(path)
    for line_number, kind, block in sentences(path):
        attributes = []
        for contents in attribute_re.findall(block):
            attributes.extend(
                item.strip().split("(", 1)[0] for item in contents.split(",")
            )
        attribute_counts.update(attributes)
        kind_counts[kind] += 1
        if path.name == "verification.k":

                if kind == "syntax"
                else "PROOF_LOCAL_EXACT_EQUATION"
            )
        elif path.name == "spec.k":
            disposition = "POSITIVE_PROOF_OBLIGATION"
        elif "no-evaluators" in attributes:
            disposition = "FIXED_OPAQUE_UNUSED_NO_DEPENDENT_CLAIM"
        elif line_number in used.get(rel, set()):
            disposition = "FIXED_USED_REVIEWED_FAITHFUL"
        elif kind in {"syntax", "configuration"}:
            disposition = "FIXED_DECLARATION_OR_CONFIGURATION"
        else:
            disposition = "FIXED_OUT_OF_PATH_NO_REACHABLE_MATCH"
        if "no-evaluators" in attributes:
            opaque.append(f"{rel}:{line_number}")
        if "priority" in attributes:
            priority.append(f"{rel}:{line_number}")
        all_sentences.append(
            (rel, line_number, kind, block, attributes, disposition)
        )

out: list[str] = []
out.append("# Exhaustive K source sentence inventory")

out.append(f"- `[priority]` sentences: {len(priority)}")
out.append(f"- `[no-evaluators]` opaque declarations: {len(opaque)}")
out.append(f"- `[simplification]` attributes: {attribute_counts['simplification']}")
out.append(f"- `[functional]` attributes: {attribute_counts['functional']}")
out.append("")
out.append("Attribute-token counts: " + ", ".join(
    f"`{name}`={count}" for name, count in sorted(attribute_counts.items())
))
out.append("")
out.append("Opaque declarations: " + (", ".join(opaque) if opaque else "none"))
out.append("")
out.append("Priority sentences: " + (", ".join(priority) if priority else "none"))
out.append("")
out.append("## Source hashes")
out.append("")
for path in paths:
    out.append(f"- `{relative(path)}`: `{sha256(path)}`")
out.append("")
out.append("## Every local sentence")
out.append("")
for rel, line_number, kind, block, attributes, disposition in all_sentences:
    out.append(f"### {rel}:{line_number} — {kind}")
    out.append("")
    out.append(f"Disposition: `{disposition}`")
    out.append("")
    out.append(
        "Attributes: "
        + (", ".join(f"`{attribute}`" for attribute in attributes) if attributes else "none")
    )
    out.append("")
    out.append("```k")
    out.append(block)
    out.append("```")
    out.append("")

OUTPUT.write_text("\n".join(out), encoding="utf-8")
print(f"inventory_output={OUTPUT}")
print(f"files={len(paths)}")
print(f"sentences={len(all_sentences)}")
print("kind_counts=" + ",".join(f"{key}:{value}" for key, value in sorted(kind_counts.items())))
print(f"priority_sentences={len(priority)}")
print(f"opaque_no_evaluators={len(opaque)}")
print(f"simplification_attributes={attribute_counts['simplification']}")
print(f"functional_attributes={attribute_counts['functional']}")
print(f"inventory_sha256={sha256(OUTPUT)}")
